statutory_reference.regulation_title: Cybersecurity Framework for Banks and Financial Institutions
statutory_reference.statutory_text_en: Unauthorized access and electronic tampering have to be controlled strictly. The mechanism has to be in place to encrypt and decrypt sensitive data traveling through WAN or public network.

obligation.description: Obligation to enforce cryptographic encryption on sensitive communications traversing public networks and WAN.

technical_control.name: Mandatory Transport Layer Security (TLS)
technical_control.description: The application must disable cleartext HTTP traffic globally and configure network security config with strict HTTPS.

observability.limitations_rationale: Static manifest and XML resource inspection fully determines cleartext permissions; dynamic network capture confirms absence of unencrypted traffic.

conditions: android:usesCleartextTraffic=true OR cleartextTrafficPermitted=true OR HTTP URL in bytecode
evidence_rule.supported_criteria: android:usesCleartextTraffic is explicitly false AND network security config enforces cleartextTrafficPermitted=false AND no cleartext HTTP endpoints invoked.
evidence_rule.non_conformance_criteria: android:usesCleartextTraffic is true OR cleartextTrafficPermitted is true OR bytecode initiates connections to plaintext http:// endpoints.
evidence_rule.insufficient_evidence_criteria: Network configuration is dynamically initialized in obfuscated native code or reflection without capture.

technical_mapping.authors_rationale: Cleartext traffic is an unambiguous violation of Section 4.1.3.12 requirement to encrypt WAN/public network traffic.

statutory_reference.regulation_title: Cybersecurity Framework for Banks and Financial Institutions
statutory_reference.statutory_text_en: The Organization shall ensure that cryptographic keys are securely generated. All materials used in the generation process shall be destroyed after usage and ensure that no single individual knows any key in its entirety or has access to all constituents making up these keys.

obligation.description: Obligation to prevent hardcoded symmetric keys and ensure secure key generation materials are destroyed.

technical_control.name: Prohibition of Hardcoded Cryptographic Keys
technical_control.description: Cryptographic keys must be derived dynamically or stored in the Android Keystore rather than hardcoded in bytecode or resources.

program_property.name: Absence of Static Cryptographic Keys in Bytecode
program_property.formal_specification: NOT EXISTS (Invoke javax.crypto.spec.SecretKeySpec(k, _)) WHERE k in StringConstants OR k in StaticByteArrays

observability.limitations_rationale: Dalvik bytecode instructions passing static literals to SecretKeySpec can be definitively detected statically.

conditions: Key argument originates from immediate instruction operand or static field
evidence_rule.supported_criteria: Cryptographic keys are retrieved via AndroidKeyStore provider (AndroidKeyStore) without static byte initialization.
evidence_rule.non_conformance_criteria: SecretKeySpec instantiated with string constant, hexadecimal byte array literal, or assets/resource file.
evidence_rule.insufficient_evidence_criteria: Key derivation occurs inside packed or encrypted native libraries (.so) not resolved statically.

technical_mapping.authors_rationale: Static keys violate Bangladesh Bank requirement that no single individual knows or has access to key constituents.

statutory_reference.regulation_title: Cybersecurity Framework for Banks and Financial Institutions
statutory_reference.statutory_text_en: Use strong cryptography and security protocols to safeguard sensitive data during transmission over open, public networks, including: only trusted keys and certificates are accepted; the protocol only supports secure versions/configurations; encryption strength is appropriate.

obligation.description: Obligation to use strong cryptography and secure protocol versions to safeguard sensitive data.

technical_control.name: Prohibition of Broken / Deprecated Ciphers
technical_control.description: Use of DES, 3DES, RC4, MD5, SHA-1 for encryption/integrity and AES in ECB mode is strictly forbidden.

program_property.name: Use of Standard Modern Cryptographic Algorithms
program_property.formal_specification: Cipher.getInstance(algo) => algo NOT IN ['DES', 'DESede', 'RC4', 'Blowfish', 'AES/ECB/PKCS5Padding'] AND MessageDigest.getInstance(algo) => algo NOT IN ['MD5', 'SHA-1']

observability.limitations_rationale: Cipher transformation strings passed to standard Java cryptographic APIs are statically observable.

conditions: Cipher string contains DES, RC4, ECB, MD5, SHA1
evidence_rule.supported_criteria: All Cipher and MessageDigest instances utilize AES-GCM, AES-CBC with HMAC, SHA-256, SHA-512.
evidence_rule.non_conformance_criteria: Invocation of Cipher.getInstance with weak ciphers or insecure modes (ECB).
evidence_rule.insufficient_evidence_criteria: Cipher algorithm string computed dynamically via reflective lookup.

technical_mapping.authors_rationale: Weak algorithms fail the regulatory mandate for appropriate encryption strength over public networks.

statutory_reference.regulation_title: Cybersecurity Framework for Banks and Financial Institutions
statutory_reference.statutory_text_en: The Organization shall appropriately protect Data-at-rest and Data-in-transit taking into consideration the level of risk.

obligation.description: Obligation to appropriately protect Data-at-rest stored on mobile endpoints.

technical_control.name: Encrypted Local Storage for Financial Data
technical_control.description: Local SharedPreferences, SQLite databases, and cache files storing account or transactional data must use EncryptedSharedPreferences or SQLCipher.

program_property.name: Protection of Local Storage at Rest

observability.limitations_rationale: Static analysis detects use of plaintext SharedPreferences vs. EncryptedSharedPreferences; dynamic inspection verifies database contents on rooted sandbox.

conditions: Sink is unencrypted SharedPreferences or standard openOrCreateDatabase
evidence_rule.supported_criteria: Usage of AndroidX Security EncryptedSharedPreferences or net.sqlcipher.database.SQLiteDatabase for sensitive fields.
evidence_rule.non_conformance_criteria: Plaintext authentication tokens or credentials saved directly into standard SharedPreferences or MODE_WORLD_READABLE files.
evidence_rule.insufficient_evidence_criteria: Storage write uses proprietary encryption wrappers whose key derivation cannot be validated.

technical_mapping.authors_rationale: Plaintext local storage of credentials directly compromises data-at-rest safeguards required by Bangladesh Bank.

statutory_reference.regulation_title: Cybersecurity Framework for Banks and Financial Institutions
statutory_reference.statutory_text_en: Data leak protections mechanism shall be implemented.

obligation.description: Obligation to prevent unauthorized data exfiltration and inadvertent backup extraction.

technical_control.name: Disable Uncontrolled Application Backup
technical_control.description: Financial applications must explicitly disable ADB backup to prevent extraction of sandbox data via adb backup.

program_property.name: Explicit Disabling of Android Backup Agent

observability.limitations_rationale: Determined strictly from AndroidManifest.xml application element attributes.

evidence_rule.supported_criteria: android:allowBackup is explicitly set to false.
evidence_rule.non_conformance_criteria: android:allowBackup is set to true or omitted (defaulting to true on targetSdk < 31).
evidence_rule.insufficient_evidence_criteria: Manifest cannot be decoded due to parser failure.

technical_mapping.authors_rationale: Leaving allowBackup enabled allows any user with physical USB access to dump the private app sandbox.

statutory_reference.regulation_title: Cybersecurity Framework for Banks and Financial Institutions
statutory_reference.statutory_text_en: The Organization shall establish baseline standards to ensure security for Operating Systems, Networks, Databases, Applications and portable devices which have to meet the organization's policy.

obligation.description: Obligation to enforce baseline application security standards before deployment.

technical_control.name: Prohibition of Debuggable Release Builds
technical_control.description: Production applications must not have the android:debuggable flag enabled in the manifest.

observability.limitations_rationale: Static manifest parsing definitively extracts the debuggable flag.

evidence_rule.supported_criteria: android:debuggable is false or omitted in release build.
evidence_rule.non_conformance_criteria: android:debuggable is explicitly set to true.

technical_mapping.authors_rationale: Debuggable release allows runtime process attachment and arbitrary memory inspection via JDWP.

statutory_reference.statutory_text_en: No person shall intentionally access or disrupt Critical Information Infrastructure (CII) without authorization.

obligation.description: Obligation to prevent unauthorized access or hijacking of Critical Information Infrastructure components.

technical_control.name: Securing Exported IPC Components
technical_control.description: All exported Activities, Services, Broadcast Receivers, and Content Providers must enforce explicit permission checks.

program_property.name: Authorization Enforcement on Exported Components
program_property.formal_specification: FORALL c IN Manifest.components: (c[exported]='true') => (c[permission] != NULL AND c[permission].protectionLevel IN ['signature', 'privileged'])

observability.limitations_rationale: Component export status and permission attributes are fully defined in AndroidManifest.xml.

conditions: exported=true AND permission attribute is missing
evidence_rule.supported_criteria: All exported components declare android:permission with signature-level enforcement.
evidence_rule.non_conformance_criteria: Application exposes unprotected exported components without permissions, allowing arbitrary external intent invocation.
evidence_rule.insufficient_evidence_criteria: Component performs internal runtime permission check in onCreate() not resolved statically.

technical_mapping.authors_rationale: Unprotected exported components permit unauthorized third-party apps to access internal app functionalities.

statutory_reference.statutory_text_en: Tampering, altering, concealing, or destroying computer program source code is prohibited.

obligation.description: Obligation to protect software against unauthorized tampering and reverse engineering.

technical_control.name: Bytecode Obfuscation and Symbol Stripping
technical_control.description: Application production bytecode must be processed with ProGuard/R8 to prevent reverse engineering.

observability.limitations_rationale: Symbol distribution and short package name patterns (e.g. a.b.c) can be calculated statically from DEX.

evidence_rule.supported_criteria: DEX packages show systematic identifier renaming (short 1-2 char identifiers, flattened packages).
evidence_rule.non_conformance_criteria: DEX contains complete, unobfuscated business logic classes and method names matching sensitive financial workflows.
evidence_rule.insufficient_evidence_criteria: Binary packing or commercial protector prevents standard DEX inspection.

technical_mapping.authors_rationale: Publishing completely unobfuscated banking bytecode drastically facilitates malicious tampering.

statutory_reference.statutory_text_en: Personal data collected must be adequate, relevant, and limited to what is necessary in relation to the purposes for which they are processed.

obligation.description: Personal data collected must be adequate, relevant, and limited to necessary requirements.

technical_control.name: Least-Privilege Android Permission Request
technical_control.description: The application must not declare dangerous permissions (e.g., READ_SMS, READ_CONTACTS, ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION) unrelated to its primary functional category.

observability.limitations_rationale: Permission presence is fully observable statically, but statutory necessity requires correlating with app business sector.

conditions: Dangerous permission declared without category justification (e.g. READ_SMS in Calculator or Flashlight)
evidence_rule.supported_criteria: App requests zero unneeded dangerous permissions; permissions strictly align with declared sector.
evidence_rule.non_conformance_criteria: Application declares high-risk permissions (SMS, Call Log, Contacts) with no sectoral justification.
evidence_rule.insufficient_evidence_criteria: Application category cannot be unambiguously identified.

technical_mapping.authors_rationale: Excessive permissions constitute prima facie evidence of non-compliance with statutory data minimization.

statutory_reference.statutory_text_en: Data fiduciaries and processors must implement appropriate technical and organizational measures to ensure security of personal data against unauthorized access, alteration, or disclosure.

obligation.description: Mandate to implement technical measures preventing unauthorized disclosure or exfiltration of personal data.

technical_control.name: Prohibition of PII Exfiltration to Insecure Sinks
technical_control.description: Personal data (IMEI, phone number, NID, geolocation) must not flow to unencrypted network sinks or public logs.

observability.limitations_rationale: Data flow reachability can be detected via static taint tracking and corroborated dynamically by packet payloads.

conditions: Taint path exists from PII source to network or log sink without cryptographic transform
evidence_rule.supported_criteria: No reachable path exists between PII sources and unencrypted external sinks.
evidence_rule.non_conformance_criteria: Identified reachable flow path where personal identifiers reach cleartext HTTP or unencrypted sockets.
evidence_rule.insufficient_evidence_criteria: Source flows into complex obfuscated reflection or native JNI boundary.

technical_mapping.authors_rationale: Transmitting PII over unencrypted channels directly violates technical safeguard obligations under Section 15.

statutory_reference.statutory_text_en: A data fiduciary cannot process personal data for purposes other than the original specified and lawful purpose.

obligation.description: Personal data must not be transferred to third-party tracking ecosystems without explicit user consent.

technical_control.name: Restricting Third-Party SDK Data Collection
technical_control.description: Third-party advertising and analytics SDKs must not automatically collect hardware and subscriber identifiers.

program_property.name: Isolation of PII from Commercial Tracking SDKs

observability.limitations_rationale: Static package attribution identifies tracker SDKs; dynamic traffic analysis observes actual telemetry payloads.

conditions: Device identifier passed directly into advertising or tracking SDK initializers
evidence_rule.supported_criteria: No advertising or analytics SDKs access persistent device identifiers.
evidence_rule.non_conformance_criteria: Tracking SDK invoked with raw hardware identifiers or dynamic traffic reveals IMEI transmitted to ad networks.
evidence_rule.insufficient_evidence_criteria: SDK uses dynamic server-side configuration to toggle identifier transmission.

technical_mapping.authors_rationale: Third-party ad networks harvesting device identifiers without consent contradicts purpose limitation.

statutory_reference.statutory_text_en: Confidentiality and integrity of personal data must be maintained during storage and transit using encryption and secure protocols.

obligation.description: Obligation to prevent leakage of personal data into operating system logs accessible to other apps.

technical_control.name: Prohibition of PII in System Logcat
technical_control.description: Personal identifiers and customer financial tokens must never be written to Android Logcat.

program_property.name: Absence of Personal Data in System Logs
program_property.formal_specification: NOT EXISTS (Invoke android.util.Log.*(tag, msg)) WHERE msg CONTAINS Source_PII

observability.limitations_rationale: Log calls in Dalvik bytecode are statically identifiable; dynamic logcat capture provides confirmatory evidence.

evidence_rule.supported_criteria: Zero logging statements emit user credentials or PII fields in release bytecode.
evidence_rule.non_conformance_criteria: Bytecode contains calls passing customer phone, password, or NID to android.util.Log.
evidence_rule.insufficient_evidence_criteria: Logging utility uses custom formatting wrapper.

technical_mapping.authors_rationale: Logcat leakage exposes personal data to all tools with READ_LOGS or desktop ADB access.
